guides.s: Check the interface format, set the endpoint, key and model name, then verify the features you need.
guides.when: You already call models in code and want to assess how moving to FathomPeak affects features and business.
guides.get: Setup essentials, candidate models and migration checks.
guides.body:
Check the API docs first, then set base_url, API key and model name. Once request fields, streaming and tool calls all work, switch production traffic.

What to check before migrating

guides.t: Schedule deferrable work and check the real cost
guides.s: Separate tasks by deadline, check resource windows and billing terms, then compare total cost.
guides.when: You have deferrable or batch tasks and want to compare the cost of different run schedules.
guides.get: Task classification, scheduling prerequisites and how to check cost.
guides.body:
Run deferrable jobs in surplus green-power windows and costs come down. When comparing prices, look at the model, resource window, deadline and quoted price together.

Check resource supply and quotes

Supply curves differ by energy type, and wind and hydro are not always cheaper at night. First browse candidate models in theModelsthen see theNodes & pricingpage for the listed terms.

Three preparation steps

1. Set task deadlines

Separate tasks that must return in real time from those that can finish later, and set the latest delivery time.

2. Verify batch run conditions

Confirm the platform supports the batch interface, queues and scheduling parameters you need, then fix the run plan.

3. Check caching and billing items

Confirm whether the model supports caching and how it is billed, and check input, output, cache and other charges separately.

Compare cost on the same basis

Cost difference = total cost of current setup − total cost of candidate setup

Run both setups on the same tasks and period, account for input, output, cache and service charges separately, then compare response quality and latency.

Checklist
  • Which tasks can wait, and what is the latest finish time?
  • Are cache support and billing basis confirmed?
  • Do you have the current quote and delivery terms?

guides.t: Choose a model with a real task
guides.s: Start from the business task and compare result quality, input types, latency and total cost.
guides.when: You have several candidate models and need to know which suits the real workload.
guides.get: Candidate directions, test dimensions and when to switch.
guides.body:
Define the task and acceptance criteria first, then compare candidates. Page categories are for a first cut and do not replace real tests.

Chat and customer service

Start with GLM or Qwen candidates and check accuracy, format and latency on real conversations.

Reasoning and planning

Evaluate reasoning models such as DeepSeek; check results on complex tasks, tool calls and cost.

Vision

First confirm the exact version supports the image input, resolution and interface you need, then check recognition on samples.

Code

Evaluate candidates such as MiniMax; check that the code runs, tool calls work and tasks complete.

When to reconsider the model

  • Quality falls short: find the failing samples, then compare candidates
  • Cost changes: check input/output length, caching and unit price
  • Latency misses target: check load and service terms, then assess switching

Current model information is in theModels.

guides.s: Deployment assessment, onboarding tests, the operations split and settlement terms.
guides.when: You want to deploy inference hardware at an energy plant or data room and set out each side's inputs and responsibilities.
guides.get: Deployment steps, responsibility checks and revenue settlement essentials.
guides.body:
The asset owner and FathomPeak first agree the site, equipment and operating plan. Once the hardware runs inference tasks, revenue, operating cost and distributable income are checked by agreement before settlement.

1. Assess site and equipment

Equipment configuration and placement are set by site, floor load, power supply and cooling.

2. Connect and test

Check electrical, network and security boundaries, and test equipment operation, model fit and task scheduling.

3. Set operations responsibilities

Task scheduling, model updatesRemote responsibilities set by agreement
Hardware inspectionInspection frequency written into the operating agreement
On-site access and power-off supportBoth sides name a site contact

4. Check revenue and settlement

First agree order metering, revenue attribution, cost deductions and revenue share, then the settlement cycle and documents. Investment returns depend on actual task volume, prices and operating cost.

guides.t: From energy supply to model service
guides.s: How plants, appliances, scheduling and model services fit together.
guides.when: You need to explain the service architecture to business, procurement or project leads.
guides.get: A four-layer explanation; formal image materials are available from sales.
guides.body:
Energy supply, task scheduling, business delivery and metering records each have their own role.

  • Equipment layer: inference hardware runs on suitable power
  • Scheduling layer: runs planned by deadline and resource status
  • Delivery layer: model service provided and settled by agreement
  • Record layer: usage, cost and energy information linked

The full architecture diagram is available from sales;.

Purchase evaluation compares cost, energy records, scope of service and migration impact separately, with tests and documents as evidence.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.bodyHtml:
Last updated: 3 September 2026
Effective date: 3 September 2026

Beijing FathomPeak Technology Co., Ltd. ("FathomPeak", "we" or "us") operates the Pinhaosuan compute–power coordination token trading platform and related services (the "Service"). We take the security of personal information and business data seriously. Please read this Privacy Policy carefully before using the Service. If you do not agree, please stop using the Service.

1. How we collect and use information

To provide a secure and stable token trading and relay service, we may process information for the following purposes:

  1. Account registration and management: We collect your mobile number, email, password, company name (if any) and similar details for registration, identification, security verification and necessary contact.
  2. Service metering and settlement: We record call time, API key identifier, token consumption (input/output), request source IP, selected model/node and billing information for billing, reconciliation, risk control and green-power statistics.
  3. Request relay: To relay API calls, we receive and forward the request content you submit. Except for troubleshooting, security audits, a history-saving feature you turn on, or requirements of laws and regulations, we do not use your business content in plaintext for secondary model training, and we do not keep it longer than necessary once the service purpose has been met.
  4. System security and operations: We collect device and log information, operation records, access frequency and error logs to keep the platform and compute nodes secure, troubleshoot faults and improve service quality.
  5. Themes and preferences: We may use cookies or local storage to remember preferences such as language and theme. You can manage cookies in your browser, but some features may be affected.

2. Sharing, transfer and public disclosure

  1. Sharing principles: We do not sell your personal information. We share necessary information, to the minimum extent, with entrusted processors, plant/node partners and upstream model providers only with your consent, to meet legal obligations, or where required to provide the Service.
  2. Forwarding to model providers: To perform the relay, your request content may be forwarded to third-party model providers that you select or that the system schedules; their own privacy policies govern how they process it.
  3. Transfer and disclosure: In the event of a merger, acquisition, asset transfer or similar, we will require the successor to remain bound by this policy. We disclose information publicly only where required by law or necessary to protect significant lawful rights and interests.

3. Storage location, retention and security

  1. Storage location: In principle, personal information we collect and generate within the People's Republic of China is stored within China.
  2. Retention: We keep information only for the shortest period necessary for the processing purpose; afterwards it is deleted or anonymised, unless laws and regulations provide otherwise.
  3. Security measures: We take reasonable measures such as encryption in transit, access control, least privilege, auditing and backups. Please keep your account and API keys safe.

4. Your rights

To the extent permitted by applicable law, you may access, correct or delete your personal information, withdraw consent, close your account, or obtain a copy of your personal information. You can submit requests through the console or customer service channels; we will handle them within a reasonable time after verifying your identity.

5. Protection of minors

The Service is intended mainly for individuals with full civil capacity and for business users. Minors should use it with the consent and guidance of a guardian. If we find that we have collected a minor's information by mistake, we will delete it as soon as possible.

6. Policy updates

We may revise this policy from time to time and publish the changes on the platform. Material changes will be highlighted more prominently. If you continue to use the Service after an update, you accept the revised policy.

7. Contact us

If you have questions, complaints or rights requests about this policy or the processing of personal information, please contact us through the customer service or contact channels published on this platform.

  • Company: Beijing FathomPeak Technology Co., Ltd.
  • Product: Pinhaosuan · compute–power coordination token trading platform
